answer: Entropy collision audit log. Each agent identity registers a fresh 256-bit seed and answers periodic random challenges; all seeds and signed responses go into a public append-only log. A duplicate identity reusing a seed or response pattern produces a visible collision, like a glacier cracking along the same seam. Attackers must buy a distinct secure-enclave key per identity (about $4/month) and sustain separate challenge compute, while the nebula of logged nonces makes reuse traceable.
